_comment: Teaching/lore NPC on the actor model (plan-entity-model.md chunk 3a) — formerly a statless model/npc type placed from zone.npcs, now an ordinary actor carrying an interaction block. role creature + speed 0 (PO 2026-07-27, D4): an NPC is an actor that authors no movement, not a kind of its own. Unattackable by two AUTHORED knobs (D5): faction townsfolk (friendlyToPlayers ⇒ player damage skips it) and collisionLayer 97 = PlayerStatic(1) + Viewport(32) + MobStatic(64) — solid and streamed, but deliberately NOT on Action(2), so no aura on either side can target it. interaction.range 2.0 [PLACEHOLDER] is the talk reach and, being the wider of the two (D7), sizes the one sensor — which is also the audience interaction.ambient fans out to. xpFactor 0 keeps it off the nameplate path; the health bar is accepted (D3). All values [PLACEHOLDER]. ⚑ D23's AMBIENT NPC and the one D18 exists for: it calls out as you walk past AND opens a tree on E; its `ambient` lines are the only ones in the game, so they are also the regression test for walk-by speech. ⚑ QUESTS: the crier OFFERS `wolves-on-the-road` but turns in NOTHING — that is D9's branch, finished east by either the CityGuard or the Shaman for different rewards; his quest brief is where the player learns there is a choice (written directions, no marker, GDD 8). ⚑ Q4 (conversation-journal §4.6): the Damage teaching is GONE — Damage is a level-1 milestone seeded at character creation now. ⚑ R4 C1 (plan-downtime.md D7/D8, 2026-08-03): the Recall teaching is GONE too — Recall is a baseline utility every character holds from creation, so the crier currently teaches nothing; the teachings node was deleted WITH its root row, because the empty-destination prune deliberately spares an authored-empty node (it reads as a lore leaf). New teachings are ordinary later content. ⚑ TEXT SHAPE (PO 2026-08-02, on top of the Q4/R1 tree shape): quest text is deliberately plain — no lore or stylized wording yet; NO quest_at_stage gates (the Q1 show-rule hides the Accept row once taken). He advances `he-who-cried-wolf` from `crier` to `governor` behind the 'Hans sends me.' row; each Dionsburg lore node repeats that advance row, which the show-rule hides outside the stage.
name: TownCrier

options.text: Hans sends me. There are a lot of wolves recently.
Do you have a task for me?
Who here has work for me?

lines: Indeed ... it's very unusual that they appear in such great numbers.
Alas, I know neither the cause nor the cure.
But maybe someone in Dionsburg knows what to do ... You should talk to its Governor about our problem.

grants.line: Splendid! Just follow the road east through the forest. It'll lead you right to the city gates.

lines: Kill 8 wolves on the west road.
Then report to the City Guard at the city gate far to the east, or to the Shaman at his fire east along the road.
Kill 8 wolves on the west road. Then report to the City Guard or the Shaman.
It's a large city to the east. It's the dwelling place of the Order of Divine Light.

grants.line: Splendid! Just follow the road east through the forest. It'll lead you right to the city gates.

options.text: Tell me more about the Order of Divine Light.

lines: It's a mighty guild of paladins, champions of the righteous cause.
They defend the city and uphold the laws in Dionsburg. They are led by a powerful paladin called Papath.

grants.line: Splendid! Just follow the road east through the forest. It'll lead you right to the city gates.

lines: Oh, I just know what everyone knows about him.
He's a champion of humanity and all of its allies against the forces of evil.
He resides in the Cathedral, in the centre of Dionsburg.

grants.line: Splendid! Just follow the road east through the forest. It'll lead you right to the city gates.

lines: Talk to Farmer Flora, Miller Reinhard, Herbalist Lionett and Shepherd Hans.
You'll find Flora and Hans to the west, Lionett to the north and Reinhard just south of here. There's always something to do.
